messages:
Alex: Quick debate — for internal service-to-service APIs (runtime <-> router <-> console backend), should we standardize on gRPC+protobuf or keep REST/JSON? Pros/cons?
Maria: I'm leaning gRPC for internal: binary, smaller payloads, built-in streaming for long-lived generation streams, strong typing.
Sam: +1 for gRPC perf, but pb maintenance + backward compatibility is a headache if we don't have a good process. Also REST is way easier for ad-hoc curl / debugging.
Leo: We should split concerns: gRPC for high-throughput runtime-to-runtime traffic, REST for any browser-facing endpoints. That avoids grpc-web for the console.
Jen: For the console we already need websockets/streaming. grpc-web + envoys works but adds complexity. Do we really want another translation layer?
Maria: If we do protobufs, we can auto-generate clients across languages, enforce schemas, and use service reflection for tools. Also easier to instrument with structured spans.
Sam: Counterpoint: JSON + OpenAPI works with almost every tool and is human-readable in logs. Many ops folks prefer being able to read payloads directly.
Alex: Operational requirements: quotas, routing policies, and telemetry need consistent headers/metadata. With gRPC we'd use metadata (x-tenant, route-id) vs HTTP headers for REST. Both fine but gateway patterns differ.
Leo: Proposal: gRPC proto-first for internal RPCs (runtime, model-pool, cache), and an API Gateway that exposes REST+JSON to public/internal console. Gateway does translation, enforces quotas, and emits unified telemetry.
Jen: Sounds good. Need to decide on tech: envoy + grpc-web + ext_auth for quotas? Or write a lightweight gateway service?
Sam: Envoy gives us rate-limiting, JWT validation, dynamic routing. But proto->openapi generation for docs becomes an extra step. We can have CI job that generates OpenAPI from protos for the console team.
Maria: Also consider versioning. Proto evolves — use minor/major versioning on package or service names. Add runtime feature flags to allow fallback to older message shapes.
Alex: Example proto snippet I was thinking of for a generation request:
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package redwood.runtime.v1;

message GenerateRequest {
  string model = 1;
  string prompt = 2;
  map<string,string> meta = 3; // routing keys, tenant
}

message TokenStream { string token = 1; }

service Runtime {
  rpc Generate(GenerateRequest) returns (stream TokenStream);
}
```
Sam: Nice. For REST gateway we'd expose POST /v1/generate with JSON body and SSE/WS for streaming tokens. Gateway responsibility: translate headers, enforce quotas, record telemetry per-token.
Jen: How do we handle partial failures? If runtime v2 returns fields console doesn't know, gateway should strip unknown fields for older clients. Proto unknown fields are preserved but in translation we can be explicit.
Maria: Another ops point: tracing. gRPC supports binary propagation via b3/tracecontext. Ensure gateway forwards trace headers for end-to-end spans.
Leo: On the topic of proto storage: central repo with autogenerated language bindings, and a publishing pipeline that tags releases. CI should block if proto changes break generated clients.
Alex: Rollout UX: prefer feature flags + staged rollouts for proto changes. Gateway can route a percentage of traffic to new service using same proto with new required fields behind flags.
Sam: One more ask: logging/debugging tools for engineers. JSON is easier for ad-hoc. Maybe gateway can log a debug-json copy of translated requests (sanitized) to a debug stream.
Maria: Agree. Also add an internal 'schema-explorer' UI that shows current proto versions and diffs — helpful during oncall.
Jen: Action items: 1) Draft proto-first spec for runtime RPCs. 2) Spike envoy gateway + grpc-web for console. 3) Add CI proto-lint + client-gen. 4) Design rollout policy docs.
Alex: I'll create the RFC doc and link a PoC repo. tagging @Maria @Sam for review.
ci-bot: Deployed preview for "grpc-gateway-poc" at https://staging.redwood.dev/ - logs in #eng-platform-ci.
Sam: thanks — will try the PoC tomorrow. :+1:
Leo: One minor note: ensure quota enforcement handles bursty prefix caching patterns — rate-limiter should be token-aware.
Maria: Good call. We'll include token accounting in the gateway metrics and surface per-route cost in the console.
Alex: ok that's the plan for now. Keep comments here and I'll convert to RFC by EOD.
